history.summary: ACTUAL LOCATION FLAG: the temple is at Arrah (Kalinagar, near Bamunara village) on Shibtala-Gopalpur Road, Durgapur 713212 - not inside Durgapur town proper; CSV town 'Durgapur' kept as the nearest city, actual locality documented here. IDENTITY PROVISIONAL: an ancient Shiva temple (also spelled Rarheswar/Rareshwar) at Arrah near Bamunara, housing a massive Shiva lingam, described as a Nagara-style temple built of sandstone and laterite. MakeMyTrip claims it was built by 'the Rarh dynasty's Maharaja Ballal Sen' in 1200 and is 'over a millennium' old; local vlogs call it an 800+ years-old temple. These claims are weakly sourced and unverified - the Ballal Sen attribution conflicts with the historical Sena chronology (Ballal Sen ruled in the 12th century, but scholarly sources for this temple were not found). The temple draws hundreds of barefoot devotees bearing water on Srabon Somvars, with prasad distribution and a local fair. Coordinates are from a map match for a Shiv Mandir at Gopalpur, Bamunara (near Arrah) - verify on the ground.

name: Rahreswar Shiv Temple (Arrah Shiv Mandir)
town_description: Arrah (also spelled Aarah) is a locality near Bamunara on the outskirts of Durgapur in Paschim Bardhaman district, West Bengal, reached via Shibtala-Gopalpur Road. The ancient Rarheswar Shiva temple at Arrah Kalinagar is the area's principal religious landmark.

travel.railway: Durgapur station, then local transport via Bamunara
travel.road: Shibtala-Gopalpur Road, Arrah Kalinagar, Bamunara, Durgapur 713212

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Shravan Mondays for the mela atmosphere
visitor_information.opening_hours: Not documented in any source found (verify). Open-access village temple; crowds peak on Srabon Somvars and Maha Shivratri.
